items.question: What's the difference between standard, certified, notarized, and sworn translation?
items.answer: Standard translation is accurate but carries no legal weight. Certified translation includes a signed statement of accuracy from the translator, accepted by most institutions. Notarized translation adds a notary's confirmation of the translator's identity. Sworn translation is completed by a translator formally authorized by a court or government body — required by certain embassies and legal proceedings. We'll confirm which classification your document needs when you message us.

items.question: Do I need to create an account or fill out a form to get started?
items.answer: No. There's no registration and no public quotation form. You simply message us on WhatsApp, send your document, and agree on scope, languages, and timeline directly with our team.

items.question: Can I rely on your certified translation with embassies and government bodies?
items.answer: Yes — our certified and notarized translations are prepared to the standard embassies, courts, and government bodies expect. We always recommend confirming with the receiving institution, and we'll help you pick the exact classification their requirements call for.

items.question: How do I know a translated document is genuinely from Bayt Languages?

items.question: What does a "revoked" or "expired" verification status mean?
items.answer: "Revoked" means Bayt Languages has withdrawn the certification for a specific reason; "expired" means its defined validity period has passed. Either way, the verification code still resolves and shows the status clearly, without disclosing further sensitive detail.

items.question: Is my document kept confidential?

items.question: How do I download my translated file securely?
items.answer: From your verification page, click the download button. If your document has PIN protection enabled, you'll be asked to enter the PIN before a secure, time-limited download link is generated.

items.answer: We translate between Arabic, English, Chinese, and a range of other languages, across a wide variety of documents — legal, medical, academic, business, government, and personal. Message us with your document's details and we'll confirm right away.

certified-vs-notarized.title: Certified vs. Notarized Translation: What's the Difference?
certified-vs-notarized.excerpt: The two terms get used interchangeably, but they mean different things — and the distinction matters when an embassy or court asks for one specifically.
body: Many people use "certified" and "notarized" translation interchangeably, but they aren't the same thing — and the distinction matters when you're submitting documents to an embassy, university, or court.

A certified translation includes a signed statement from the translator or translation provider attesting that the translation is accurate and complete. It's the most commonly requested type, and it's accepted by the vast majority of institutions — universities, employers, and many government offices.

A notarized translation goes one step further: a notary public witnesses the translator's signature, confirms their identity, and applies a notarial seal. Importantly, the notary does not verify the accuracy of the translation itself — only that the person who signed the certification statement is who they claim to be.

Some institutions, particularly certain courts, immigration authorities, and foreign embassies, specifically require notarization. Others will accept a standard certified translation without issue. The safest approach is always to ask the receiving institution directly which classification they require before requesting your translation.
At Bayt Languages, we ask this exact question at the start of every conversation on WhatsApp, so your document is prepared to the correct standard the first time — no costly redo later.

documents-that-need-certified-translatio.title: 5 Documents That Almost Always Require Certified Translation
documents-that-need-certified-translatio.excerpt: From birth certificates to corporate registers — here's why these five document types are almost never accepted as a plain, uncertified translation.
body: Certain documents carry legal or official weight, so the institutions that request them almost always require a certified translation rather than a plain one. Here are five you'll run into most often.
Birth certificates, when submitted for immigration, citizenship, or residency applications — the receiving authority needs a translation it can hold accountable, not an informal rendering.
Marriage certificates, typically needed for spousal visas, name-change procedures, or family reunification cases abroad.
Academic transcripts and diplomas, required by universities for admissions and by professional licensing bodies verifying your qualifications.
Powers of attorney and other legal instruments used across borders, where an error in translation could change the legal effect of the document.
Corporate documents — articles of incorporation, commercial registers — needed to open a foreign bank account or register a branch office.

If you're not sure whether your document needs certification, message us on WhatsApp with a description of the document and where it's going. We'll confirm the right classification before any work begins.

how-long-does-certified-translation-take.title: How Long Does a Certified Translation Take?
how-long-does-certified-translation-take.excerpt: There's no single answer — length, language pair, and classification all affect the timeline. Here's how to think about it realistically.
body: There's no single answer to how long a certified translation takes — it depends on the document's length, the language pair, and the classification you need.
A short, standard document — a birth certificate or national ID — with a common language pair is often turned around within one to two business days once our team confirms scope.
Longer documents, like contracts or multi-page academic transcripts, take longer, since every page goes through translation and then an independent review before delivery.
Notarized or sworn translations can add time, since they depend on a notary's or authorized translator's availability in addition to the translation itself.

The most useful thing you can do is message us with your document's page count and your deadline upfront. Our team will give you a realistic timeline on WhatsApp — before any work begins, and before you're committed to anything.
There's no online quote form for a reason: a person on our team actually looks at your document before quoting a timeline, rather than guessing from a form field.

choosing-a-translation-partner.title: How to Choose the Right Translation Partner for Legal Documents
choosing-a-translation-partner.excerpt: Not all translation providers are equipped for legal work. Here's what to actually check before you send over a contract or court document.
body: Legal documents carry consequences that a casual translation doesn't — so choosing the right partner matters more than it does for, say, a marketing brochure. Here's what to look for.

Specialist terminology. Look for translators who work specifically with legal language, not general bilingual staff. Legal terms rarely have a single obvious equivalent across languages, and a mistranslated clause can change a contract's meaning.

Independent review. Ask whether every translation goes through a second linguist before delivery. A single-pass translation, however skilled the translator, carries more risk for wording that needs to be exactly right.

Correct classification. Confirm how the provider classifies and certifies a translation — standard, certified, notarized, or sworn — and whether that classification is one the specific institution you're dealing with will actually accept.
Confidentiality. Legal documents often contain sensitive personal or commercial information. Ask directly how a provider protects your documents and who has access to them.

Verifiability. Can the receiving institution independently confirm that a delivered translation is authentic and hasn't been altered since delivery? This is exactly the gap our QR-verifiable certificate closes — every completed translation ships with one, at no extra step for you.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains how Bayt Languages collects, uses, and protects information in the course of providing certified translation services.

sections.heading: Information we collect
sections.body: We collect information you share with us directly — such as your name, contact details, and the documents you send for translation — through WhatsApp conversations. We also collect basic technical data (such as browser type) when you visit this website or a verification page.

sections.heading: How we use information
sections.body: Information you share is used solely to scope, deliver, and support your translation, and — where you request it — to generate a digital verification certificate for the completed document.

sections.heading: Document confidentiality
sections.body: Documents you send us are handled under strict confidentiality and are only accessible to the translator, reviewer, and administrative staff assigned to your job.

sections.heading: Data retention
sections.body: We retain your documents and related records for as long as necessary to deliver our services and to support the ongoing validity of any verification certificate issued.

sections.heading: Your choices
sections.body: You decide how your name appears on a public verification certificate — shown in full, partially masked, or hidden entirely. Contact us at any time to ask a question about your information.

sections.heading: Our services
sections.body: Bayt Languages provides standard, certified, notarized, and sworn translation services. There is no public quotation form, file upload, or online payment on this website — every engagement begins with a direct conversation on WhatsApp.

sections.heading: Engagement process
sections.body: Scope, languages, classification, timeline, and pricing are agreed directly between you and our team before any translation work begins. Competitive pricing is confirmed on request and is not published on this website.

It remains your responsibility to confirm with the receiving institution that the classification we've prepared (standard, certified, notarized, or sworn) meets its specific requirements.

sections.heading: Changes to these terms

confidentiality.title: Confidentiality Policy
confidentiality.intro: Confidentiality is central to how Bayt Languages handles every document entrusted to us.

sections.heading: Our commitment
sections.body: Every document and every detail you share with us is treated as strictly confidential, from the moment you send it on WhatsApp through final delivery.

sections.heading: Access control
sections.body: Only the translator, reviewer, and administrative staff directly assigned to your job can access your document. Documents are never shared internally beyond what a job requires.

sections.heading: Visibility on verification certificates
sections.body: You choose how your name appears on your document's public verification page: shown in full, partially masked, or hidden entirely. Internal notes and staff identities are never shown publicly, regardless of your choice.

sections.heading: Secure storage

sections.heading: Third parties
